question: In the clinical examination of a surgical swelling, assessment of regional lymph nodes is optional and can be omitted if the swelling appears benign.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct. Always examine the regional lymph nodes, regardless of how innocent the swelling looks. Missing nodal metastases or lymphadenitis due to an apparently benign primary swelling is a significant clinical error.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: This is false. Regional lymph node examination is mandatory for every surgical swelling. Nodal enlargement may be the first indication of malignancy or spreading infection even when the primary swelling appears benign.
